chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Two men brought a dispute to Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him). One of them had bought a camel from the other, and the seller had excluded the head and the skin. Then the buyer decided to sell it, so he (peace be upon him) said to the buyer: 'He is your partner in the camel, according to the measure of the head and the skin.'
ai.seo_question: What is the legal status of excluded parts in a sale contract if the buyer resells the item?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the mechanics of partial exclusion (istithna') in commercial transactions, establishing that excluded parts retain the seller's ownership while the buyer holds a proportional share. It highlights the precision of Shia jurisprudence in distinguishing between full transfer of ownership and retained fractional rights, ensuring clarity in subsequent resale or partnership scenarios. The ruling underscores the importance of explicit stipulation in contracts to prevent disputes over residual assets.
